title: Armenia’s births fall, deaths rise in 2025
content: Armenia's birth rate declined by 6.3% in the first eight months of 2025 compared to the same period in 2024, according to the National Statistical Committee, with 20,437 births recorded versus 21,821 in 2024. The number of stillbirths fell by 17.2% year-on-year to 256 cases. Meanwhile, deaths increased by 0.8% to 17,210, leading to a drop in the vitality index—the ratio of births to deaths—from 127.8% in 2024 to 118.8% in 2025. The leading cause of death remained diseases of the circulatory system, accounting for 51.8% of fatalities (8,908 people), a 2.3% decrease from 2024. Neoplasms (cancers) were the second most common cause, responsible for 19.5% of deaths (3,360 people), down 2.7%. Respiratory diseases caused 10.5% of deaths (1,802 people), a 12.4% increase, while deaths from digestive system diseases declined by 10.3% to 804. External causes, such as accidents and injuries, accounted for 3.6% of deaths (620 people), down 10.3%. However, deaths from endocrine disorders rose by 16.3% to 364, and fatalities from infectious diseases surged by 46.5% to 233. These trends reflect Armenia’s ongoing population decline driven by low fertility and mass emigration, a pattern observed across the Emerging Europe region.

title: Демографический кризис в Армении углубляется: рождаемость падает, смертность растет
content: Armenia is experiencing an deepening demographic crisis, with declining birth rates and rising mortality. According to the National Statistical Committee of Armenia, 20,437 children were born between January and August 2025—a 6.3% decrease compared to 21,821 births in the same period of 2024. The decline in births has persisted since the beginning of 2024 and continued throughout 2025. During the same period, there were 256 stillbirths, a 17.2% decrease compared to the previous year. Meanwhile, mortality increased by 0.8%—17,210 deaths were recorded in January–August 2025, up from 17,065 in the same period of 2024. The leading cause of death was circulatory system diseases (51.8%, or 8,908 deaths), a 2.3% decrease. Cancer (19.5%, or 3,360 deaths) ranked second, down 2.7%. Deaths from respiratory diseases rose by 12.4% (1,802 cases, 10.5% of total), and from endocrine diseases by 16.3% (364 cases, 2.1%). Infections increased sharply by 46.5% (233 cases, 1.3%). Deaths from digestive system diseases and external causes both fell by 10.3% (804 and 620 cases, respectively). The vitality index—births per deaths—dropped to 118.8% in January–August 2025, down from 127.8% in the same period of 2024.

title: В Армении за первые 7 месяцев этого года зарегистрировано 42 убийства
content: Armenia recorded 42 murders in the first seven months of 2025, according to data released by the National Statistical Committee. This is an increase from 32 murders in the same period of 2023. For the full year, 63 murders were registered in 2024, compared with 55 in 2023. The same period also saw 44 attempted murders in 2025, versus 63 in 2024 and 55 in 2023. Firearm‑related crimes totaled 72 in the first seven months of 2025, down from 109 in 2024 and 93 in 2023. The Ministry of Internal Affairs reported that the number of murders in the last eight months fell by two to 32 cases, excluding suicides, sudden deaths, accidents, and cases identified from previous years. 'За этот же период снизилось число тяжких и особо тяжких преступлений, совершенных с применением огнестрельного оружия: в 2025 году - 93 случая, в 2024 году - 100 случаев', – the ministry said.

title: Проходит 5 лет с ракетного обстрела Арменией Барды
content: On October 5, 2025, it marked five years since Armenian armed forces launched a rocket attack on the city of Barda during the 44-day Patriotic War, which began on September 27, 2020. On October 5, 2020, two rockets struck central streets and the central hospital of Barda, killing two people and injuring six others, while causing massive damage to civilian infrastructure. Barda District was shelled five times during the war—on October 5, 8, 27, 28, and November 7—resulting in 29 civilian deaths (including two children and eight women) and 112 injuries. On the same day, Armenian forces also attacked Ganja, Azerbaijan’s second-largest city, firing rockets from the Berd region. The rockets hit the Ganja International Hospital, School No. 34, a furniture factory on Shah Ismail Khatai Street, the 'Evlakh Bus Terminal' area, and the central market, injuring three people and causing significant damage. Ganja was attacked five times between October 4 and 17, resulting in 26 deaths and 175 injuries. On October 5, 2020, two rockets were fired at Beylagan, one landing in a kindergarten courtyard and the other in an open area. On that day, Barda, Ganja, Beylagan, as well as Geranboy, Goygol, and Terter districts were also targeted. According to the Azeri Press Information Agency, Armenia violated the Geneva Conventions by attacking civilians, committing war crimes. Throughout the war, Armenia used ballistic missiles and heavy artillery to attack Evlakh, Beylagan, Terter, Gabala, Geranboy, Agdjabedi, Khizi, and other cities and districts. The attacks resulted in 93 civilian deaths (including 12 children and 27 women) and 454 injuries. A total of 12,292 residential and non-residential buildings and 288 vehicles were damaged. Criminal cases were opened under relevant articles of the Criminal Code of Azerbaijan.

title: Обнародовано число смертей за последние 7 месяцев в Азербайджане
content: The State Statistics Committee of Azerbaijan reported that 34,994 deaths were registered in the country during the first seven months of 2025. The death rate per 1,000 residents remained unchanged at 5.9 compared with the same period in 2024, according to the agency. The report states, 'По сравнению с аналогичным периодом 2024 года показатель на каждые 1000 человек населения остался неизменным -- на уровне 5,9'.

title: По данным за первые восемь месяцев 2025 года, по сравнению с предыдущим годом число убийств снизилось. МВД
content: Armenia's Ministry of Internal Affairs (MVD) announced at a press briefing that the number of murders recorded in the first eight months of 2025 fell by 2% compared with the same period in 2024. Press secretary Narek Sargyan said, 'Хочу отметить, что по данным за первые восемь месяцев, число убийств сократилось на 2% по сравнению с прошлым годом. В целом снизилось число преступлений, совершённых с применением огнестрельного оружия', – подчеркнул Саргсян. He added that overall crimes involving firearms also decreased. The MVD representative countered rumors that the country’s shooting situation is uncontrollable, stating, 'Подавляющее большинство этих случаев стрельбы связано с уголовными делами, имеющими признаки хулиганства, и в основном касается выстрелов из пневматических пистолетов или случаев стрельбы в воздух. Утверждать, что ситуация в стране крайне неконтролируема, - голословное утверждение', – заявил представитель МВД. According to the MVD, police seized almost twice as much illegal firearms and ammunition in the first eight months of 2025 as they did in the same period of 2024.

title: Arminfo: Температура воздуха в Армении повысится еще на 3-5 градусов - прогноз синоптиков
content: According to the Center for Hydrometeorology and Monitoring of the Ministry of Environment of Armenia, the temperature in Armenia is expected to rise by 3-5 degrees. The weather forecast for the period from August 20 to 24 indicates that the regions of the country will experience dry weather. The wind will be southwesterly, with gusts of up to 2-5 m/s. On August 20-22, there may be an increase in wind gusts up to 15-18 m/s in the Ararat Valley, Vayots Dzor, Aragatsotn, and Kotayk regions, as well as in Yerevan. The high level of fire hazard will persist in these areas. In Yerevan, the temperature is expected to be 36-38 degrees Celsius during the day on August 20, 27-29 degrees Celsius in the evening, and 20-22 degrees Celsius above zero at night on August 20-21.

title: Погода в Армении: резкое потепление
